preconditions: The web and bot services must be deployed with the shown host naming so the bot's FLAG cookie is scoped to the web host.
An attacker must be able to submit a report URL to the bot service.
An attacker must operate a callback URL accepted by navigator.sendBeacon.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: Inner markup begins an HTML comment and invokes navigator.sendBeacon(callback, document.cookie).
trigger_steps.summary: Receive the beacon body emitted by the inner same-origin script after the bot visits the reported page.

impact.affected_asset: FLAG cookie scoped to the web host in the administrator bot browser context.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the reporting bot to visit a crafted web URL and receive document.cookie at an attacker-controlled callback endpoint.
impact.security_effect: Same-origin script execution in the administrator bot's browser followed by disclosure of its web-host FLAG cookie through a beacon request.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies an ASCII html query value no longer than 1024 characters to the web endpoint.

The service checks a fixed dangerous-element list in a parse5-backed Cheerio tree, serializes it, reparses that serialization with htmlparser2-backed Cheerio, and checks the second tree; the organizer payload combines noembed, textarea, and plaintext markup with a script source and is constructed to pass this parser-differential pipeline.

After the second intermediate-tree tag check, the service sends the second serialization directly as text/html. The organizer solution uses the resulting document to load a same-origin script URL whose supplied markup invokes navigator.sendBeacon with document.cookie.
The reporting path makes Chromium visit the supplied URL after setting a FLAG cookie for the web host; the organizer receiver treats the beacon POST body as the obtained flag.

failure.operation: Directly serving the htmlparser2-derived serialization after parser-specific dangerous-tag checks.

primary_invariant.statement: No browser-executable or embedding element may be introduced into the HTML document served to the browser from attacker-controlled markup.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Safety is decided from dangerous-tag membership in two different intermediate Cheerio parse trees, while parser-specific serialization and subsequent browser parsing can yield a browser-effective document not represented by those checks.

quality.review_notes: Primary service, bot, report-endpoint, and organizer-solution artifacts establish a concrete end-to-end oracle contract, but this bundle contains no execution transcript proving a run. No implemented remediation patch is supplied; mitigation is a derived invariant-restoration target. Cookie disclosure is challenge-specific because the shown FLAG cookie is readable by page JavaScript.

remediation.invariant_restored: The document delivered to the browser must be produced and checked under one policy such that no executable or embedding construct can be reconstructed after validation.
mitigation_classes: eliminate parser/serializer differentials in the validation-to-render path
validate or sanitize the final browser-effective document with a single unambiguous HTML policy
avoid serving attacker-controlled markup as active HTML

target.component: web/double-parser web service and administrator bot

oracle.expected_negative: After removing the parser-differential reconstruction path or preventing active attacker HTML from being served, the callback receiver should not receive the FLAG cookie for the supplied crafted payload.
oracle.expected_positive: A deployment reproducing the supplied pipeline and bot behavior would cause the organizer solution's callback receiver to log a request body containing the bot document.cookie value after it reports the crafted web URL.
